prompt:
Lexical ambiguity: Lexical ambiguity occurs when a word has multiple meanings, making its interpretation dependent on the context. It can arise in two forms: (1) when a word has unrelated meanings despite sharing the same spelling and pronunciation, it is called homonym (e.g.,"bank" as a financial institution vs. "bank" as the side of a river). These meanings originate from different etymology root (2) when a word has related meanings that stem from a single etymology, it is referred to as Polysemy (e.g.,"green" referring to the color and to something environmentally friendly).
